about: Trust scenarios (E2EE spec §8) run through both clients: test_kybot.py Scenarios (kybot.py) and web/src/crypto/trustScenarios.test.ts (engine.ts). Each side builds the scenario by name and must report exactly expect. Members a_dana (devices d1, d2), the sender, a bot of Dana's in a later lookup batch behind 99 filler members.

scenarios.name: removal_seen_late
scenarios.says: The batch naming Dana shows her old list (d1, d2); the later batch with her bot shows her newer list without d2. d2 gets no room key.

scenarios.name: stale_list_in_later_batch
scenarios.says: The batch naming Dana shows her newer list (d1 only); the later batch with her bot shows the older one (d1, d2). The older list counts for nothing and blocks nothing: d1 gets the room key, d2 does not.

scenarios.name: identity_conflict_across_batches
scenarios.says: Dana is pinned. The batch naming her shows her pinned key; the later batch with her bot shows another key. Dana is blocked: nothing goes to her devices or her bot.

scenarios.name: delisted_fresh_mail
scenarios.says: Dana removes d2 from her list (its row and cross-signature stay). d2 then tries to send a room key: the server refuses it and nobody reads it.

scenarios.name: delisted_delayed_mail
scenarios.says: d2 sends a room key while listed; Dana removes d2 before the recipient reads its mail. The key is still read (owner decision 28 Nov 2026: a removed device's earlier mail stays deliverable).
